headline: A Saudi national and former OpenAI engineer has been arrested in San Francisco, accused of hiding a recorder in an OpenAI conference room.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the arrest ran in our 14 Oct edition and the court appearance was on 13 Oct; this adds charge details.
importance_line: It shows AI labs are treated as national security targets for spying, which concerns the labs and the US government, though the allegations come from a complaint and no court has tested them.
source: Downbeach.com, citing the US Justice Department complaint
summary: Downbeach.com reports, citing the Justice Department's complaint, that Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, is accused of hiding an encrypted audio recorder behind a television in an executive conference room at OpenAI's San Francisco office. He is charged with intercepting oral communications and faces up to five years in prison if convicted; the allegations are untested, and the arrest was in our 14 Oct edition.
notes: Duplicate story of our 14 Oct item (C13-02 there); this adds details and the suspect's name.
